rationale: Standard ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ 'king' used here in the parable of the wise craftsman who works for his master = the king. In line 28 the parable-king is identified with ⲡⲛⲁⲃ ⲛⲣ̄ⲣⲟ 'the great king' = the Third Ambassador. The mapping confirms a typological reading: craftsman:king :: Father of Life:Third Ambassador.

Greek τεχνίτης 'artisan, craftsman.' Paired here with native Coptic ⲍⲁⲙϣⲉ 'craftsman' as a doublet-couplet (cf. analogous Greek-Coptic doublets in this corpus). 'Artisan' preserves Greek register distinct from 'craftsman.'

Greek ἀργόν substantivized — 'idle, unworked, raw.' Standard term for raw material before craftsmanship. The unworked wood without imprint is the parable's image of the cosmos before the Father's shaping wisdom acts upon it.

Reduplicated intensive form of ⲗⲱⲃϣ 'mingle, blend' (in glossary). The reduplication intensifies to 'thoroughly mingled/molten' — the metallurgical phase of the craftsman parable. Distinct from non-intensive ⲗⲱⲃϣ in cosmogonic texts.

Hapax-like form in this corpus. Context (paired with ⲗⲱⲃⲗⲱⲃϩ 'melting' and the action of filling/multiplying) supports a smelting-vessel/crucible reading. Possibly Greek βαφή 'dipping-vat' or related to a native term for forge-vessel.
Greek-derived vessel-name (possibly κάδος, κήβος, κάβος) listed alongside ⲫⲓⲁⲗⲏ 'bowl' and ⲭⲁⲡ 'lid' as types of wooden vessels produced by the parable craftsman. Tentative identification as 'jar.'
Possibly Coptic ϫⲁⲡ 'cover, lid' or a vessel-component term. Final item in vessel-triad jar/bowl/lid. Tentative.
